task.name: A story that raised the preflight scope decision is scored below the threshold on resume, so the decision is neither answered nor defaulted but silently skipped
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A sprint story raised the preflight complexity gate on one run and was dispatched straight
to implementation on the resume of that same run, having been scored differently the second
time.

On the first run, at 09:09:26, the preflight complexity gate fired for `issue-2684` and
logged `Complexity: 9 (impl 9, validation 1) ≥ threshold 9`. It paused the story, offered
`approve` and `decompose` with a one-hour window defaulting to `decompose`, and printed a
decomposition assessment proposing three candidate slices together with three design
questions it recorded as unsettled. Nothing had been spent on the story beyond preflight.

The run was stopped before the window elapsed, and was later resumed with the original
invocation plus `--resume`.

On the resumed run there is no preflight complexity gate line for that story, or for any
other story in the sprint. The persisted routing artifact for the story was written at
12:04:38, during the resumed run rather than carried over from the first, and records an
implementation complexity of 8, a validation complexity of 1, a total of 8, and no scope
exception. Both runs recorded the same story content hash, and the issue body was not
edited between them. The threshold is 9.

The story went to implementation without the gate being raised a second time. The pending
scope decision was not answered by the operator, was not resolved to its stated `decompose`
default, and was not carried forward; it simply did not recur. The resulting change spans
3,965 insertions across 25 files and implements all three of the slices the decomposition
assessment had proposed as separate work, resolving each of the three questions it had
recorded as unsettled. It entered review having spent roughly twice its own recorded
dev cost estimate.

## Expected behavior

A preflight verdict is a property of the story it scored, so evaluating the same story
content must yield the same verdict every time it is evaluated. A score that straddles its
threshold cannot depend on which run performed the scoring, because a gate whose answer
changes between evaluations of identical input is not a gate — a re-run becomes a way to
obtain the permissive answer, and the more expensive the story, the more likely something
interrupts and re-runs it.

Separately and independently of determinism, a decision the system has solicited from the
operator is either answered, resolved to its stated default, or raised again. It is never
discarded. A run that resumes across an unanswered decision must arrive at one of those
three outcomes for it, so that proceeding at full scope is something the operator chose
rather than something a second evaluation quietly permitted. Where the resumed evaluation
would reach a different conclusion than the one that raised the decision, that divergence
is itself the thing the operator needs put in front of them, not a reason to skip asking.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `a7297712813cb7d054269f0399881ba451864e13` captured at `2026-09-12T00:34:12.792463+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/sprint/dag.py` — `sha256:8dfeb8d54535af0e23d0bc805bcfd72f307282488fe900f1296b715bd5c3ec1a`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:2f6c562595efc644eec33ba96e1e1403ef435598e966e320f7a570564e66e587`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/run_setup.py` — `sha256:ad64336ae78973bb413e258075d9a96e4e496c174b1d37eddaed41c82c0850c4`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py` — `sha256:d2b4ff9deeb3aaa9377ea917969a8b8c977a40b7b262ea334430a5e52ce4f9be`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_complexity_gate.py` — `sha256:76dbb7db38ca954322f52f7945f9a4d9a7ff307dc06c3f83941ce2e7c0bf319f`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/resume_persistence.py` — `sha256:4e7b8ecee9bb88de22bae54f5b2a9d8cff6167d370dfd6b1852e9a90e7247951`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_cache.py` — `sha256:c55430010e98809494910c1a28127be0caf618d3b6041c44a46bb321151997aa`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight.py` — `sha256:283d3626ffe00fc1c389cad585fec268d712a2aa4e649c142405d9d00c108aa0`
- `docs/guides/controller-runbook.md` — `sha256:8ee116442c692be19c50bb76f15241ea1b0859f04eeca994b5f0da6241c85b4d`
- `CONVENTIONS.md` — `sha256:236f37038716fab82e3992564460dd0af7366cb3e6d7c8f855c1430d3caca9bb`
- `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2860-36eb64db9dc8.yaml` — `sha256:f9ba1a9a021638e5aa2fce6b2b61815f01434b7e094999d1bc6e05d64d289086`

### Observed symptom

A sprint story (issue-2684) whose PREFLIGHT run opened the PREFLIGHT complexity gate
(score 9 vs threshold 9), left the operator's approve/decompose decision unanswered,
and was killed before the decision window elapsed, was resumed via the same invocation
plus `--resume`. On resume, no PREFLIGHT complexity gate line appeared for this or any
other story; the story's persisted routing artifact from the resumed run showed a
recomputed complexity of 8 (impl 8, validation 1) for the identical story content hash,
no scope_exceeded, and the story proceeded straight through planning/implementation. The
pending decision (and the decomposition assessment/unsettled questions it carried) was
never answered, never resolved to its stated `decompose` default, and never re-raised —
it was silently discarded, and the story landed a change implementing all three
previously-proposed slices at roughly 2x its own recorded dev cost estimate.

### Reproduction / evidence

Issue #2860's own attached evidence: first-run log at 09:09:26 — "Complexity: 9 (impl 9,
validation 1) ≥ threshold 9" — followed by a pending record offering approve/decompose
(1-hour window, default decompose) and a decomposition assessment (3 slices, 3 unsettled
questions). The run was killed before the window elapsed. On `--resume`, no gate line
appears for this or any story; the routing artifact for issue-2684 at 12:04:38 (the
resumed run) shows implementation complexity 8, validation 1, total 8, scope_exceeded
false — under the threshold of 9. The story landed 3,965 insertions across 25 files,
implementing the three proposed slices.

Source-verified mechanism, traced end to end at HEAD:
- A story interrupted during PREFLIGHT (as in this repro — the process was blocked
  inside the gate's operator poll, so no dev commit ever landed) leaves its worktree
  with zero commits ahead of the base branch.
- `_triage_spec` (src/theforge/sprint/dag.py:417-426) classifies a worktree with 0
  commits ahead as `action="full"`, explicitly discarding the worktree reference
  (`worktree_path=None`) with the comment "run_task WORKSPACE phase will recreate it
  from scratch."
- The sprint dispatcher (src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:2288-2329) only routes
  `triage.action == "review"` to `run_from_review` and `triage.action == "dev"` to
  `run_from_dev` — both of which end up in `_run_resume_coordinator`/`_setup_resume_entry`,
  the ONLY call site (src/theforge/coordinator/run_setup.py:694, imported at
  engine.py:214) that invokes `recover_phase_state`/`apply_resume_record_to_state`
  (src/theforge/coordinator/resume_persistence.py:1237, 1177) to restore a prior
  attempt's preflight/gate state onto the resumed `CoordinatorState`. Any other
  triage action, including `"full"`, falls through to the `else` branch at
  runner.py:2328, which calls `_run_fresh` → `run_task`.
- `run_task` (src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:1097) allocates a brand-new
  `_fresh_run_state()` and contains no call to `recover_phase_state` or
  `apply_resume_record_to_state` anywhere in engine.py (grepped: zero references
  outside `run_setup.py`/its resume-entry caller). PREFLIGHT is then executed live
  and unconditionally via `_run_preflight_phase` with a state that carries none of
  the first run's `preflight_complexity_gate_opened`, `preflight_complexity_gate_decision`,
  or `preflight_complexity_gate_assessment` — those fields never existed on this
  process's state at all, not merely "lost to a short-circuit."
- `should_gate()` (src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_complexity_gate.py:192-207)
  evaluates purely against `state.preflight_complexity_score` as freshly computed
  this run. `evaluate_preflight_complexity_gate()` (same file, lines 755-756) returns
  `None` immediately when `should_gate()` is False — before ever reaching the
  "honour the recorded decision" branch at line 764 — but for this exact repro that
  branch would have found nothing anyway, since `run_task` never populated
  `preflight_complexity_gate_decision` from the interrupted first attempt in the
  first place.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** A story stopped mid-PREFLIGHT (0 commits ahead of base) is triaged to `action="full"` on resume and dispatched through `run_task`, which never invokes the resume-record recovery machinery (`recover_phase_state` / `apply_resume_record_to_state`) that only `run_from_dev`/`run_from_review` (triage actions "dev"/"review") wire up — so the resumed PREFLIGHT re-executes as a fully independent live evaluation with zero memory of the interrupted gate, the pending decision, or the assessment already produced.
  - Evidence: Traced directly in source: dag.py's zero-commits-ahead branch returns `action="full"`, `worktree_path=None`, with a comment stating run_task will recreate the workspace from scratch. runner.py's resume dispatcher branches only on `action in {"review","dev"}` before falling through to `_run_fresh`/`run_task` for anything else. `recover_phase_state` is called from exactly one place (`_setup_resume_entry` in run_setup.py), itself called only inside `_run_resume_coordinator`, which backs only `run_from_dev`/`run_from_review`. `run_task` (engine.py) contains no reference to either recovery function. `should_gate()`/`evaluate_preflight_complexity_gate()` then evaluate a state that never carried the prior gate's decision/assessment fields, so a freshly recomputed score below threshold silently drops the story straight to planning.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All cited control flow (dag.py, runner.py, run_setup.py, engine.py, preflight_complexity_gate.py) was read directly in the repository at HEAD. None of it restates a prior diagnosis's conclusion — a prior diagnosis for this same issue (.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2860-36eb64db9dc8.yaml, dated 2026-09-02) cited a different, no-longer-present code comment in runner.py as its supporting premise anchor, which this investigation confirmed absent at current HEAD before tracing the mechanism independently through the triage/ dispatch layer instead.
- **[ruled out]** should_gate()'s lack of a fallback to a previously-recorded gate decision is itself the point where the decision is lost (i.e., the decision exists on state but the gate's control flow discards it).
  - Evidence: For this repro, the decision was never on the resumed state to begin with — `run_task` never restores any resume-record fields, so `state.preflight_complexity_gate_decision` is `None` for a structural reason (the recovery call site is never reached for a "full" triage), not because `should_gate()`'s early return skips past a populated field. The prior-decision branch in `evaluate_preflight_complexity_gate` is dead code for this exact symptom instance; fixing only that branch's placement, without also reaching the triage/dispatch gap, would not restore anything to check against.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read directly in engine.py/run_setup.py/preflight_complexity_gate.py at HEAD.
- **[confirmed]** The gate's opened/decision fields are only persisted after the operator poll completes or times out, so a process killed mid-poll leaves no durable trace of the open gate to recover even if recovery were wired up for this triage path.
  - Evidence: `_record()` (preflight_complexity_gate.py:436-465), which sets `preflight_complexity_gate_opened`/`_decision`, is called by `evaluate_preflight_complexity_gate` only after `_open_gate()` returns (line 791-809) — i.e., after the poll resolves or times out. The only persistence call inside `_open_gate` itself, `_persist_gate_state` at line 936, runs before polling and saves only the decomposition-assessment fields (via `_record_assessment`), not `opened`/`decision`. A run killed while blocked in `poll_pending` (as in this repro — "stopped before the window elapsed") therefore never persists that the gate was opened or what was decided. This is a contributing precondition (there would be nothing to recover even on a triage path that called recovery) but is separate from, and does not by itself explain, why this story's dispatch path skips recovery entirely.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read directly from preflight_complexity_gate.py at HEAD; not a restatement, though the prior diagnosis for this issue reached the same conclusion about this specific sub-point independently.

### Confirmed cause

A story interrupted during PREFLIGHT before any dev commit exists (as when a process
is killed while blocked in the complexity gate's operator poll) leaves its worktree
with zero commits ahead of the base branch. `_triage_spec` (src/theforge/sprint/dag.py)
classifies such a worktree as `action="full"` and discards the worktree reference,
intending `run_task`'s WORKSPACE phase to recreate it from scratch. The sprint's resume
dispatcher (src/theforge/sprint/runner.py) routes only `action in {"review","dev"}`
through `run_from_review`/`run_from_dev`, which are the only paths that reach
`_setup_resume_entry` → `recover_phase_state` → `apply_resume_record_to_state` — the
machinery that restores a prior attempt's PREFLIGHT judgement, its complexity-gate
opened/decision/assessment fields, and the pending scope decision onto a resumed
`CoordinatorState`. Every other triage action, including `"full"`, falls through to
`run_task`, which allocates an entirely fresh `CoordinatorState` and never calls that
recovery machinery anywhere in its own code path. PREFLIGHT is then re-executed as a
brand-new, independent live LLM evaluation carrying zero memory of the interrupted
gate — not merely a score recomputed differently, but a `CoordinatorState` that never
held the prior decision, the prior assessment, or even the fact that a gate had opened.
When that fresh evaluation happens to score the same story content below the
threshold, `should_gate()` returns False and the story proceeds straight to
planning/implementation, because there was never anything recorded on this run's state
for the gate to check, honour, default, or re-raise.

Support: Directly observed and traced end to end in source at HEAD: dag.py's zero-commits-ahead
branch (`action="full"`, `worktree_path=None`); runner.py's resume dispatch branching
only on `action in {"review","dev"}` before falling to `_run_fresh`/`run_task`;
run_setup.py's `_setup_resume_entry` as the sole call site of `recover_phase_state`;
its sole caller `_run_resume_coordinator`, itself reachable only from
`run_from_dev`/`run_from_review`; and confirmation by exhaustive grep that
`engine.py`'s `run_task` contains no independent call to `recover_phase_state` or
`apply_resume_record_to_state`. These are five distinct call sites in four different
files, all read directly, that converge on one gap without any of them stating this
issue's conclusion for me to restate.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All cited call sites were read directly in the repository at HEAD. A prior diagnosis of this same issue (.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2860-36eb64db9dc8.yaml, 2026-09-02) reached a related but less precise conclusion (should_gate's early return, framed around a runner.py comment that is no longer present in the codebase) — this investigation independently re-derived the mechanism through the triage/dispatch layer rather than relying on that prior report's premise anchor.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/sprint/dag.py:417-426 (`_triage_spec`'s zero-commits-ahead → action="full"
branch, which discards the worktree reference for any story with no dev commit yet);
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:2288-2329 (resume dispatch routes only "review"/"dev" to
the recovery-aware paths, falling through to `_run_fresh`/`run_task` otherwise);
src/theforge/coordinator/run_setup.py:577-723 (`_setup_resume_entry`, the sole caller
of `recover_phase_state`); src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py (`run_task`, which never
calls `recover_phase_state`/`apply_resume_record_to_state`); and
src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_complexity_gate.py:192-207, 740-789 (`should_gate`
and `evaluate_preflight_complexity_gate`, which act correctly on whatever state they
are given but are given a state with no memory of the interrupted gate for this
dispatch path).

### Fix-success criterion

For a story whose PREFLIGHT run opened the complexity gate and left the operator's
decision unresolved when the process stopped — including the case where the
interruption happened before any dev commit existed, so the worktree shows 0 commits
ahead of base — resuming that same run must not silently dispatch the story to
planning/implementation at full scope. The resumed attempt must arrive at one of:
(a) honouring an operator answer recorded in the interim, (b) applying the configured
no-decision default and recording that it did so, or (c) re-opening the pause and
asking again — regardless of which dispatch path (triage "full" vs "dev"/"review")
the resume takes, and regardless of what score a freshly re-executed preflight happens
to compute for identical story content. A resumed evaluation that would reach a
different (in particular, a lower, sub-threshold) score than the one that originally
opened the gate must have that divergence surfaced to the operator rather than
silently treated as the gate never having applied.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- preflight_complexity_gate_opened/decision are only persisted to the resume record after the operator poll completes or times out (_record(), called post-_open_gate). Even on a dispatch path that does call recovery (dev/review triage), a process killed mid-poll leaves the record showing complexity_gate_opened=false — a durable "opened, undecided" marker would be needed for recovery to have anything useful to restore for this exact repro shape.
- _merge_phase_blocks's foundation comparison in resume_persistence.py has no signal for two equally-founded preflight attempts that disagree on the score itself; it always lets the incoming (later) attempt's block win. Relevant to preflight score non-determinism generally, but distinct from this issue's triage/dispatch gap.

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Not verified as a full design. Two independent gaps both need to close for the fix to
be complete, and either alone is insufficient: (1) `_triage_spec`'s "full" outcome for
a zero-commits worktree should still check for and carry forward a durable resume
record when one exists for that slug — a story can have a fully valid, evidence-backed
resume record (preflight completed, gate opened, assessment generated) despite having
made no dev commits, and today's "0 commits ahead → discard and start over" logic
conflates "no dev commits" with "nothing durable to recover." (2) Separately, per the
prior diagnosis of this issue,`preflight_complexity_gate_opened`/`_decision` are only
persisted after the operator poll resolves; persisting an "opened, undecided" marker
durably before/during polling (not just the assessment) would make the record above
actually contain something to recover from a kill-mid-poll scenario, since today, even
with recovery wired up, this exact repro's record would show `complexity_gate_opened:
false` and no decision to restore — the resumed evaluation would still need to
independently re-derive "this story was previously gated" from the presence of a
restored `preflight_complexity_gate_assessment_generated=true` combined with no
recorded decision, and treat that combination as an outstanding decision to re-raise
rather than as "gate never applied."

### Notes

This diagnosis supersedes the prior diagnosis attempt for this same issue
(.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2860-36eb64db9dc8.yaml, run 36eb64db9dc8, 2026-09-02,
which landed with `partial: true` and a `LAND failed` lifecycle-state error rather
than being applied). That attempt's confirmed_cause centered on should_gate()'s
current-run-only score check, supported in part by a runner.py comment
("A story already past preflight gets a *fresh* live preflight attempt on resume")
that this investigation confirmed is absent from runner.py at current HEAD — the
prior report's own `unchecked_premises` already flagged this pattern as unverified
against baseline. This investigation independently re-derived a more precise
mechanism (the triage/dispatch gap: `action="full"` stories never reach the
resume-record recovery machinery at all) that is consistent with, and explains,
every piece of evidence in the issue, without relying on that absent comment.
This report does not extend to redesigning preflight for determinism — the issue
text explicitly frames determinism and decision-durability as separate,
independently-necessary properties, and this report scopes to the decision being
discarded (the issue's stated symptom).

outcome.message:
preserved work predates conflicting commits on release/v0.16

The preserved reused worktree at /Users/pwickersham/src/theforge/.forge/worktrees/issue-2860 holds 2 commits made before 2 commits landed on release/v0.16. Replaying the preserved work on top of origin/release/v0.16 conflicts, so this story cannot resume from it as-is. The worktree itself is intact — the rebase was aborted and nothing was lost.

Files changed on both sides:
  - src/theforge/coordinator/audit_storage.py
  - tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v49.json
  - tests/test_coord_policy_provenance_seam.py
  - tests/test_decomposition_acceptance_seam.py
  - tests/test_knowledge_receipt_seam.py

release/v0.16 commits that changed those files:
  - f82d7a5f A run identity is keyed inconsistently across canonical and preserved audit trees, so one run can be indexed twice, indexed under the wrong path, or overwritten by a thinner payload (#3009)

Available resolutions:
  - Bring the work forward yourself: rebase /Users/pwickersham/src/theforge/.forge/worktrees/issue-2860 onto origin/release/v0.16 (git rebase origin/release/v0.16) outside forge, resolve the conflicts there, commit, then resume the sprint — the resume will find the worktree already current.
  - Discard the preserved work and re-run the story from current release/v0.16: git worktree remove --force /Users/pwickersham/src/theforge/.forge/worktrees/issue-2860 (and delete its branch), then resume — the run recreates the worktree from origin/release/v0.16. Any work in it is lost.
  - Leave it and drop the story from the sprint if the release/v0.16 commits above already supersede the preserved work.

Resolving the conflicts in place with git rebase --continue is not a supported operator action here: the run does not resume a worktree left mid-rebase.

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 introduces an originating gate run identifier and original pending deadline on state, but CoordinatorState and resume_persistence.py use explicit field/block mappings and are not listed among the files to modify. Also, pending.read_pending removes a HITL record whose original PID is dead, so the resumed lookup cannot use that reader unchanged.
  Suggestion: During implementation, either explicitly reuse the resume record's top-level run_id and read timeout_at through a stale-safe pending-record path, or add dedicated fields plus serialization/restoration in state.py and resume_persistence.py. Ensure the answered-pending resume test uses a dead original PID so it exercises the real interruption case.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 says the gate overlay applies 'when the recovered record matches the same story_content_hash', but validate_resume_record (resume_persistence.py:749) is the plan's validation entry point in Step 3 while the story_content_hash lives in preflight_cache_snapshot (preflight_cache.py:34-59); the plan does not say which of the two checks authorizes the overlay, and preflight_cache_snapshot may not be present on a record whose snapshot capture never ran.
  Suggestion: Have the dev settle on one authorization: validate_resume_record against the TaskStory content as the gate-overlay predicate, treating a missing preflight_cache_snapshot as 'non-gate fields not reusable' rather than 'gate not recoverable', so an absent snapshot cannot silently disable the fix.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 introduces new state/record fields (originating gate run_id, original pending deadline, gate-scoped prior score) that must round-trip through resume_persistence's explicit field list — _record_state_block (resume_persistence.py:182-225) and _apply_preflight (991-1040) enumerate every complexity_gate_* key by hand, so a new field added only to CoordinatorState will not persist.
  Suggestion: Add the new keys to both the write list in resume_persistence and the restore tuple list in _apply_preflight, and assert round-trip in the Step 4 seam test that 'an open gate writes a resume record before poll resolution'.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's normalization of recovered preflight states for downstream consumers (compute_bundle_assignments, synthetic-edge computation, scheduler-decision stamping) is phrased as 'verify that ... or normalized using the existing resumed-story footprint precedent' — an instruction to check rather than a decided behavior.
  Suggestion: Pick the footprint-normalization path by default (reusing the _recovered_story_footprint precedent at sprint/runner.py:1996) and fall back to tolerant reads only where a field has no recorded source.
